personas.description: You build Apex, Flow, or API customizations for Salesforce Order Management and want to show your development experience.

personas.label: Integration engineers
personas.description: You connect Order Management with systems such as a warehouse, ERP, or shipping provider, and design how those systems exchange data.

personas.label: Technical consultants

examDifficulty.heading: How difficult was the Order Management Developer AP exam?
examDifficulty.summary: Salesforce no longer offers this exam. Before registration closed, it tested hands-on Order Management development, including APIs, Apex, Flow, and integrations. Candidates needed to understand how these parts work together in a customer implementation.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 90 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
70% to pass, which is 42 correct answers out of 60.
Technical work: The guide covered data management, platform development and integration, Order Management, and Omnichannel Inventory.
Retirement: Registration ended July 24, 2026, and the last exam date was August 31, 2026. Salesforce plans to retire the credential on February 1, 2027.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: For future study of Order Management development, use Salesforce documentation and build small examples with Apex, Flow, and integrations. The exam is no longer available to book or take.

examFormat.heading: What was the Order Management Developer AP exam format?
examFormat.intro: Salesforce has ended registration and exam delivery. The official guide listed 60 scored multiple-choice questions, up to five unscored questions, 90 minutes, and a 70% passing score. The credential is scheduled to retire on February 1, 2027.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: The guide covered Order Management data and domain knowledge, platform development and integration, reference implementations, Omnichannel Inventory, and advanced use cases. Questions asked candidates to apply these skills to customer requirements.
bestWayToPass: Review the Order Management APIs: Learn which APIs create or update order data and how to handle errors in Apex.
Practice automation and integration: Build a Flow or Apex action and connect it to another system using an appropriate platform feature.
Understand fulfillment: Follow how order data moves from capture through allocation, fulfillment, shipping, and returns.
Plan for testing and scale: Test expected and error paths, and make sure code handles batches of records within platform limits.

certificationCard.description: This guide covers Order Management development topics such as order data, Apex, Flow, integrations, and fulfillment.

keyConcepts.h2: Order Management Developer AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Order data and APIs
blocks.body: Order Management uses related records to represent an order and its later activity. Learn how order data is imported, converted, queried, and updated. Salesforce APIs can create records in real time. Choose an API that fits the data and integration need, and handle errors so failed requests can be investigated or safely retried.

blocks.heading: Automation and platform development
blocks.body: Use Flow for supported low-code automation and Apex when the requirement needs custom code. Apex actions can be called from Flow and other Salesforce features. Keep automation bulk-safe, and test both successful work and failures.

blocks.heading: Integrations and order management design
blocks.body: An Order Management project may connect Commerce, payment, invoicing, warehouse, or other systems. Map what each system does and when it sends or receives data. Use platform features such as triggers, events, and notifications where they fit the integration.

blocks.heading: Reference frameworks and historical data
blocks.body: The exam guide included Salesforce reference implementations and frameworks for importing historical orders and resolving customer records. Learn what each framework supports before recommending it; a framework does not replace the need to map the customer’s data and process.

blocks.heading: Omnichannel Inventory and advanced cases
blocks.body: Omnichannel Inventory helps coordinate availability across locations and channels. Consider how it connects with Order Management and Commerce. The guide also covered more involved requirements such as bulk orders, fraud detection, and remorse periods.

scenarioTips.h2: How to study Order Management development topics
scenarioTips.intro: The exam is no longer available. These study notes follow the topics in Salesforce’s Order Management Developer exam guide.

blocks.heading: Order data and APIs
blocks.body: Practice importing historical order data and creating records through APIs. Know how to choose between available approaches and how to check the result.

blocks.heading: Platform development
blocks.body: Build a small Apex action that can be used from Flow. Test normal results, errors, and bulk inputs.

blocks.heading: Platform integration
blocks.body: Map the information that Commerce, payment, and external systems send or receive. Consider timing, error handling, and which platform feature fits each connection.

blocks.heading: Reference implementations
blocks.body: Review Salesforce’s listed frameworks for historical imports, customer record resolution, and B2C Commerce use cases. Be ready to explain what each one is designed to support.

blocks.heading: Omnichannel Inventory
blocks.body: Study how inventory availability connects to Order Management and Commerce. Match the design to the customer’s channels, locations, and order process.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer places one order for items stored at different warehouses. Which feature decides where each item should go?
options: The account record’s preferred warehouse for the customer
A product setting that assigns every unit to one warehouse
A manual order split created by a support agent
Order routing that allocates items to fulfillment locations
sampleQuestions.explanation: Order routing can allocate items to locations based on the order and available fulfillment choices.
whyWrong: The account’s preferred warehouse does not make item-level allocation decisions.
A fixed product location cannot respond to each order’s fulfillment needs.
Manual splits do not provide scalable order routing.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a fulfillment order represent in Salesforce Order Management?
options: A customer invoice for goods that have arrived
A payment authorization created when the order is submitted
A request to return goods after delivery
The items that one fulfillment location must process
sampleQuestions.explanation: A fulfillment order groups the items that a location is responsible for fulfilling.
whyWrong: An invoice is a separate financial document.
Payment authorization is a payment step, not a fulfillment record.
A return uses return-related records and processes.

sampleQuestions.question: A buyer cancels one item from an order with three items, before shipping. What should the system do?
options: Cancel the full order and ask the buyer to place it again
Update the order summary to reflect the cancelled item
Ship the item and wait for the buyer to return it
Issue a credit but leave the order data unchanged
sampleQuestions.explanation: The order can be amended to remove the cancelled item while the other items continue.
whyWrong: Cancelling the full order also affects items the buyer still wants.
Shipping the cancelled item ignores the buyer’s request.
A credit alone leaves the order records out of sync.

sampleQuestions.question: Which description best fits an order summary?
options: A record of the order’s current state and later changes
A permanent copy of the order exactly as first submitted
A shipping label for each package leaving a warehouse
A list containing only payments captured for the order
sampleQuestions.explanation: The order summary reflects the order as it moves through changes and fulfillment.
whyWrong: The original order record preserves the initial submission.
A shipping label is used to ship a package.
Payment records track payment activity separately.

sampleQuestions.question: A developer must run logic as soon as an order changes to a certain status. Which approach fits?
options: Run a scheduled job that checks every open order each night
Use a validation rule to prevent the status change
Use a record-triggered Flow or Apex for the status change
Ask a support agent to review each status update
sampleQuestions.explanation: A record-triggered Flow or Apex can respond when the order status changes.
whyWrong: A nightly job delays the response and checks records that may not have changed.
A validation rule blocks a change instead of responding to it.
Manual review is not an automated response.

sampleQuestions.question: An integration retries a payment request after a network timeout. Why should it use an idempotency key?
options: An order is limited to one payment record for its entire life
The retry should not charge the customer a second time
The payment service requires requests in one fixed sequence
Apex cannot make a callout more than once
sampleQuestions.explanation: An idempotency key helps the payment service recognize a retry and avoid processing the same payment twice.
whyWrong: An order can have more than one payment-related record.
Request ordering is a separate integration concern.
Callouts can be retried; the retry must be safe.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer returns one discounted item from an order. What should the refund amount be based on?
options: The full order total, including every shipping charge
The item’s current list price on the day of the return
A fixed percentage of the original order total
The amount paid for that returned item
sampleQuestions.explanation: The refund should reflect the amount paid for the returned item, including any applicable discount.
whyWrong: Refunding the entire order would include items the customer kept.
The current list price may differ from the amount originally paid.
A fixed percentage may not match the item’s paid price.

sampleQuestions.question: What information does an order delivery group provide?
options: Items that will be delivered together to one address
Carriers approved for a particular sales region
Warehouses that hold stock for each product
The required processing order for fulfillment records
sampleQuestions.explanation: A delivery group associates items with a delivery destination and method.
whyWrong: Carrier approval is configuration, not the group’s purpose.
Inventory records track stock by location.
A delivery group does not set the processing sequence.

sampleQuestions.question: A promotion causes many orders to arrive at once. What should a developer check in custom Apex?
options: Whether the org has enough fulfillment locations configured
Whether each order can be processed in its own transaction
Whether the code handles records in bulk
Whether automation should be disabled during the sale
sampleQuestions.explanation: Bulk-safe code can process groups of records while respecting Apex limits.
whyWrong: More locations do not fix code that processes records inefficiently.
Separate processing for each record can exceed limits at high volume.
Disabling automation can leave orders incomplete.

sampleQuestions.question: In Order Management, what does order capture mean?
options: Charging a payment method after the goods have shipped
Recording delivery confirmation from the carrier
Creating an order from a customer purchase
Assigning ordered items to fulfillment locations
sampleQuestions.explanation: Order capture creates the order in Salesforce from the customer’s purchase.
whyWrong: Charging a payment method is a separate payment action.
Delivery confirmation happens after shipment.
Allocation follows capture as part of fulfillment.

sampleQuestions.question: A location cannot fulfill an item because it has no stock. What is a suitable next step?
options: Cancel every item on the order and notify the customer
Reallocate the item to another location that can fulfill it
Ship the other items and omit the unavailable item without notice
Keep the order on hold without a status update
sampleQuestions.explanation: If another location can fulfill the item, reallocation can keep the order moving.
whyWrong: Cancelling every item may be unnecessary if only one is unavailable.
Omitting the item without telling the customer creates a service problem.
An unexplained hold leaves the customer and staff without useful status.

sampleQuestions.question: Why might a developer publish a platform event when an order changes?
options: To let other systems react without coupling them to the order process
To calculate the refund due for each returned item
To enforce validation rules on order summary records
To store order history for external systems to query later
sampleQuestions.explanation: A platform event lets subscribers react to a change without the publishing process needing to know each subscriber.
whyWrong: Refund calculation is business logic, not the purpose of an event.
Validation rules govern record changes directly.
An event is a message, not a queryable history store.

sampleQuestions.question: Which statement explains the difference between an order and its order summary?
options: A user creates the summary manually, while Salesforce creates the order
The order summary is maintained as the captured order moves through its lifecycle
Only customers can see the summary, while only staff can see the order
The summary is for subscriptions, while orders are for physical goods
sampleQuestions.explanation: The order summary is the managed record used to represent order activity after capture.
whyWrong: Both records are created as part of the order process.
Who can see a record depends on access settings.
The distinction does not depend on whether goods are physical.

sampleQuestions.question: An order has shipped and is with the carrier. The customer asks to change the delivery address. What is the realistic response?
options: Contact the carrier because editing Salesforce will not redirect the parcel
Edit the summary and assume the carrier receives the new address
Cancel the shipped fulfillment order to recall the parcel
Add a delivery group to redirect the parcel already in transit
sampleQuestions.explanation: Once the parcel is with the carrier, changing a Salesforce record does not redirect it.
whyWrong: Editing a record does not automatically change the carrier’s shipment.
Cancelling a shipped fulfillment order does not recall the parcel.
A new delivery group would not redirect a parcel already in transit.

sampleQuestions.question: Which task is Salesforce Order Management designed to support?
options: Running the online storefront where buyers browse products
Preparing financial statements for recognized revenue
Managing orders from capture through fulfillment and returns
Operating warehouse equipment inside a distribution center
sampleQuestions.explanation: Order Management supports the order lifecycle, including capture, fulfillment, changes, returns, and refunds.
whyWrong: A storefront is provided by Commerce or another sales channel.
Financial statements are prepared by finance systems and processes.
Warehouse equipment is handled by warehouse systems.
